product_one_liner.value: Trusaic provides pay-equity and pay-transparency compliance software for global employers, analyzing and remediating compensation disparities and streamlining regulatory reporting.
product_one_liner.notes: The official homepage describes PayParity as software to analyze, remediate, and prevent pay inequities for enterprises and lists reporting and transparency products. This supports the concise description of the suite and its employer audience.

pricing_page.notes: The official homepage navigation and footer list solutions, resources, careers, contact, and demo links but no pricing link; the checked pricing path did not return a pricing page. Under the question’s rule, this supports false.

named_customers.notes: named_customers: Trusaic’s case studies identify Boston Beer Company and Mother Jones as PayParity customers. | named_customers.0: The case study names Boston Beer Company and describes its relationship with Trusaic. | named_customers.1: The case study names Mother Jones and states that it turned to Trusaic for a pay-equity audit.

employee_band.notes: The Trusaic LinkedIn company profile reports 122 employees, which falls in the requested 101-200 band.

hq_location.notes: hq_city: The Trusaic LinkedIn company profile places its locality in Los Angeles, California; combined with the same profile’s United States country field, the headquarters city is Los Angeles. | hq_country: The Trusaic LinkedIn company profile identifies the country as United States and the locality as Los Angeles, California.

founded_year.notes: The Trusaic foundation excerpt explicitly dates Trusaic to 2014. The company biography separately dates its predecessor First Capitol Consulting to 1999, which explains the distinction; 2014 is the stated foundation of Trusaic.

eng_blog.notes: The blog index lists topical compliance and marketing articles; within its AI section it shows only one post framed as a behind-the-scenes product-build article. That single post is by CEO Robert Sheen, not a series of two or more engineering-authored technical posts, so it does not meet the engineering-blog threshold.

public_docs.notes: The homepage’s navigation and footer expose the blog, resources, product pages, and trust center, but no Docs, Help, or developer-portal link. Its trust center provides security/compliance materials rather than a multi-article public product help/documentation center, supporting false under the specified rule.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: The readable Trusaic job-board listing reports one current opening and identifies it as Sales Development Representative, not an AI, ML, or data-science role. No qualifying current AI/ML position was listed.

compliance_certs.notes: compliance_certs: Trusaic’s homepage trust-and-security badges name SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 Certified, and GDPR Compliant. These are the listed certifications/compliance claims; CCPA is not one of the requested options. | compliance_certs.0: The homepage explicitly names SOC 2 Type II. | compliance_certs.1: The homepage explicitly names ISO 27001 as certified. | compliance_certs.2: The homepage explicitly says GDPR compliant.

last_funding.notes: funding_stage: The Tracxn profile describes Trusaic as unfunded, so the schema’s required stage value for no known outside funding is "none".

raised_18mo.notes: The current Tracxn profile identifies Trusaic as unfunded, so there is no outside funding round in the preceding 18 months.

hiring_sdr_ae.notes: The Trusaic Sales Development Representative posting was listed online October 31, 2026, shortly before the reference date, indicating current SDR hiring.

launched_6mo.notes: Trusaic announced an enhanced EU Pay Transparency Directive Transposition Monitor with an interactive map on May 20, 2026. This product-feature announcement falls within the six months before November 9, 2026.

leadership_change_12mo.notes: The public leadership page lists the company’s leadership roster, and the dated March 2026 Ireland expansion announcement describes local hires and an adviser appointment rather than a C-level or VP-level appointment. No announcement or profile found in the 12-month window identifies a C-level/VP join or departure; the small roster supports false, with some uncertainty because the page does not state every start date.

crm_stack_signal.notes: crm_stack_signal: A Trusaic sales-development posting names HubSpot and Salesforce as CRM tools and ZoomInfo as a sales prospecting/data system. The official site also uses a HubSpot meeting link. These are visible stack signals from the requested source types. | crm_stack_signal.0: The sales-development posting names HubSpot as a CRM signal; the company site also routes demo scheduling through HubSpot. | crm_stack_signal.1: The sales-development posting explicitly names Salesforce as a CRM tool applicants should know. | crm_stack_signal.2: The sales-development posting explicitly names ZoomInfo for sales prospecting.
